extracted.intended_audience: authors, editors, proofreaders, indexers, and publishing production professionals
extracted.subtask_description: Style and production guidelines for preparing, editing, and publishing books, journals, and electronic publications (manuscript preparation, typography, citations, illustrations, indexes, and front/back matter).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclamation points (usage)
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on use and punctuation of exclamation points, including related forms such as exclamatory questions and inverted exclamation in other languages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uses: editorial interpolation (to be avoided); with ellipses (in Russian); exclamatory questions; generally; with introductory oh or ah; inverted in Spanish works; in mathematical expressions; in titles of works; cross-reference to exclamations and interjections. Also cross-references to punctuation interactions (commas, quotation marks, parentheses, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fair-use doctrine
rubrics_metrics.description: Overview and practical guidelines for fair use in publishing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes legal overview and Chicago’s guidelines; covers attribution, Creative Commons licenses, dissertations and theses; general rules and 'rules of thumb'; relation to photocopying and unnecessary permissions; treatment of specific materials: charts/tables/graphs, data in tables, epigraphs, illustrations, interior monologues, interviews, paraphrasing, pictorial/graphic material, unpublished works. Cross-references: acknowledgments; illustration credits; source notes; permissible changes to quoted and referenced materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: File formats and devices (requirements)
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for file formats and devices for different publication types and content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance for e-books, electronic supplementary data, journal and magazine article formats, multimedia, illustrations, and publications in multiple formats; mentions functional features, hyperlinks, metadata, terminology and punctuation specific to formats; testing and submission guidelines; and special notes for unpublished documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Version control: file-hosting services
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of file-hosting services for version control in manuscript and production workflows.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: File-hosting services recommended as part of version-control practices; see references to electronic file cleanup and production checklist for implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: File naming conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Formatting and typographic guidelines for file names associated with artwork, proofs, and production files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes required extensions, format for file names in production checklist, file names for proofreading, slashes in file names, typographic considerations, and version-control naming conventions. Cross-references: file formats and devices; electronic file cleanup.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figures: definition, citation, and references
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition of figures and guidance on source citations and text references to figures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines figure usage and the term; guidance on abbreviation of the term; specifying source citations for figures; how to reference figures in text and conventions for numbering and callouts. Cross-references: artwork, captions, illustrations, tables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Footnotes: formatting and use
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for footnotes including numbering, length, continuation across pages, and comparison with endnotes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers continued footnotes across pages, editing and proofreading of footnotes, pros and cons vs endnotes, use of endnotes with footnotes, keying to line or page numbers, examples and figures, indexing of footnotes, length considerations, manuscript preparation guidance, not always used in electronic publications, numbering conventions, overview and source-note practice for previously published materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Front matter: contents and formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: What belongs in front matter and how to format front-matter elements for books and journals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists standard front-matter elements: acknowledgments; author’s signature; biographical notes; chronologies; copyright information; dedication; editorials; epigraph and epigraph source; forewords; frontispieces; half-title page; list of contributors; lists of abbreviations; lists of illustrations and tables; half-title and table-of-contents conventions; pagination and placement; submission and production checklist items; differences for electronic publications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fonts and typefaces: selection & proofreading
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on choice, permissible changes, and proofreading practices for fonts and typefaces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes on archaic type, fonts for computer terminology, embedded fonts, fonts for digital artwork and mathematical copy, Gothic (Fraktur), old-style numbers vs full-size caps, serif vs sans serif, specialized fonts for non-English materials, permissible changes, proofreading of typefaces, and punctuation interactions. Cross-references: typographic considerations; Unicode standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Galleries: illustration placement and numbering
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidelines for galleries (collections of plates/images) within a publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Callouts generally not needed for gallery images; how galleries appear in lists of illustrations; manuscript preparation guidelines; numbering illustrations in galleries; placement and pagination; plates in galleries; inclusion in table of contents; unpaginated galleries; thumbnails and index considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Glossaries: format, alphabetizing, and linking
rubrics_metrics.description: Formatting rules for glossaries and how glossary entries should be handled in print and electronic publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Boldface for defined terms appearing in the glossary; format and alphabetizing rules; format of terms; hyperlinks to glossaries; relation to indexing and placement in the book; punctuation and submission practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Global changes in editing and proofreading
rubrics_metrics.description: Policy and practice regarding global changes applied during manuscript editing and proofreading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mentions global changes as part of manuscript editing and proofreading workflows; guidance references to electronic file cleanup and marking/managing global replacements, with notes about proofreading implications and when global changes are appropriate or risky.

rubrics_metrics.name: Headings: placement, punctuation, and proofreading
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidelines for headings in various parts of a publication and punctuation conventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of headings for chronologies, endnotes, indexes, letters and diaries, lists of abbreviations, lists of illustrations and tables; navigation headings in electronic publications; headings with note numbers; proofreading and punctuation of headings; treatment in reference lists. Cross-references: subheads; index entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Headline-style capitalization
rubrics_metrics.description: Principles and applications of headline-style capitalization for titles and headings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides principles and examples for headline-style capitalization across chapter and part titles, journal and magazine article titles, newspaper headings, mottoes, and subheads; treatment of hyphenated compounds and non-English words; guidance for permissible changes and reference-system exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hyphens and hyphenation (guide and manuscript concerns)
rubrics_metrics.description: Comprehensive rules for hyphenation, hyphenated compounds, and related manuscript/typographic considerations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers capitalization interactions, hyphenation in compound terms (with detailed guide), -ly adverbs, compound modifiers, en dash vs hyphen, suspended hyphens, trend toward closed compounds, vs dashes, manuscript marking and proofreading procedures, software settings, non-English language exceptions, personal names, readability considerations, uses in fractions/URLs/dates/source citations, and guidance for hard vs soft hyphens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hyperlinks: use, markup, and testing
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for use of hyperlinks in printed and electronic publications and for metadata and markup.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of hyperlinks for DOIs, errata, e-book formats, illustrations, tables, tables of contents, home pages, retractions, and related works; cross-checking and testing of hyperlinks; markup guidance for HTML and PDF; metadata considerations; hyperlinking in indexes and source citations; guidance on adding hyperlinks to printed work and for errata/retractions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hyperlinks in source citations
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance specific to including hyperlinks (and DOIs/URLs) in bibliographic source citations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advantages and annotation conventions; checking and consistency requirements; interaction with author-date systems and shortened citations; use in journals; relation to footnotes vs endnotes; metadata linkage; source notes for previously published material; tables usage; and cross-references to DOIs and URLs in citations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Illustrations: acquisition, preparation, permissions, and reproduction
rubrics_metrics.description: Comprehensive standards for acquiring, preparing, crediting, and reproducing illustrations and artwork.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accessibility issues, acquisition types (adapted, commercial agency, commissioned, obtained free, previously published, public-domain, made-for-hire), illustration credits and credit lines (content, placement, editing), electronic files preparation (prints vs scans, file formats, separate files for components, identification), as electronic supplementary data, numbering and conventions, indexing of illustrations, hyperlinks to illustrations, keys/legends, thumbnails, reproduction issues (cropping/scaling/shading, halftones, scans), permissions and photo releases, plates and types of illustrations (color, line art, halftone), submission to publisher and proofreading, and relation to running heads and tables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Illustration credits and credit lines: content and placement
rubrics_metrics.description: What illustration credit lines must contain and where they should appear.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contents: adapted material, author’s own work, commercial agency material, commissioned material, cover/jacket artwork, maps; editing of credits; format of credit lines; importance of credits; placement (copyright page, cover or jacket, list of illustrations and tables, back matter); proofreading; and relation to permissions and public-domain works.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indexes: construction, placement, and quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on creating indexes, their placement, format, length, and quality control.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes that automatic generation is not possible; editing and proofreading of indexes; examples; electronic-publication considerations; hanging (flush-and-hang) indentation vs indented style; headnotes and headnote use; continued lines and runover lines; length and publisher preferences; order of multiple indexes; placement in the book; repagination issues; quality standards and checks to perform.

rubrics_metrics.name: Index entries: locators, subentries, punctuation, and alphabetizing
rubrics_metrics.description: Detailed rules for composing index entries, locators, cross-references, and subentry structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appropriate use of locators and checking; chapter numbers with locators; avoidance of ff and et seq.; italics and boldface usage for locators; handling long strings of locators; locators for notes and paragraph numbers; punctuation rules in index entries; cross-references; alphabetizing of main headings and subentries; use and formatting of subentries and sub-subentries; indentation and run-in vs indented styles; when to use or avoid sub-subentries; dealing with vanity entries; and checking procedures for index quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusive (continuing) numbers: formatting and use
rubrics_metrics.description: How to format and use inclusive or continuing number ranges (pages, dates, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abbreviating and condensing inclusive numbers; interaction with abbreviations and symbols; commas with inclusive numbers; dates formatting across contexts; use of en dashes in ranges; full-style and condensed-style options; handling in index entries and tables; unfinished ranges; use with percent and repeated quantities; roman-numeral behavior and tables treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: House style: implementation and editorial practice
rubrics_metrics.description: How a publisher's house style is enforced and integrated into editorial and proofreading workflows.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Author communications on house style; editing for house style; application in indexes, source citations, and tables; proofreading for house-style consistency; use of style sheets and publisher preferences; relation to production checklists and house-specific source-citation practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gender and bias-free language
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on avoiding bias and handling gendered language in editorial practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoiding bias in language; capitalization rules for gendered terms; necessary gender-specific language and pronoun guidance; personal identification and non-English personal names; pronoun use and inclusive-language recommendations; cross-reference to bias-free language.
